conditions.description: The workload container is explicitly configured with privileged: true.
conditions.rationale: Privileged containers receive broad host capabilities and defeat normal container isolation assumptions.

conditions.description: The container explicitly runs as UID 0.
conditions.rationale: Running as root increases the impact of a container compromise and weakens least-privilege posture.

conditions.description: The pod mounts the host root directory through a writable hostPath volume.
conditions.rationale: The container can directly modify host filesystem state through /host.

conditions.description: The pod explicitly automounts its service-account token while also running with broad host privileges.
conditions.rationale: A compromise can combine workload credentials with host access, increasing blast radius.
This is an explicit filesystem-hardening control and should not be falsely reported as absent.

conditions.description: The container declares CPU and memory requests and limits.
conditions.rationale: Resource limits are present and should not be reported as missing.

conditions.description: Whether admission policy blocks privileged pods or hostPath usage in the target cluster is not established by this manifest.
conditions.rationale: Admission enforcement is a cluster-side control requiring external evidence.

conditions.description: The actual RBAC permissions granted to the pod service account are not established by this Deployment manifest.
conditions.rationale: No Role, ClusterRole, or binding artifacts are present.

conditions.description: The workload must not be cleared as least-privileged or strongly isolated from the host.
conditions.rationale: privileged root execution plus writable host root access contradicts such a clearance.

conditions.description: The workload must not be cleared as having a minimal credential blast radius.
conditions.rationale: A service-account token is mounted, while its RBAC scope remains unknown and the container has broad host access.
